data.title: Agent Memory
data.tagline: A mechanism for an Agent to save and retrieve selected information in later interactions; its scope depends on the product and settings
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish current conversation history, project rules, and cross-session memory, then check what a new conversation actually loaded.
data.description: While coding, you want the Agent to avoid automatically editing shared components. The same conversation may retain chat history; a new one sees the preference only if project rules are read or a supported memory is saved and retrieved. Check what the new conversation actually loaded in the target project.

learning.assumes: You have seen an AI stop referring to earlier instructions after a conversation restarts.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish current conversation history, project rules, and cross-session memory, then check what a new conversation actually loaded.

distinctions.label: Conversation history
distinctions.explanation: Conversation history stores messages from a conversation; the system can provide them again when continuing the same conversation. Retention and continuation depend on the product's session mechanism.

distinctions.label: Project rules
distinctions.explanation: Project rules are files or settings stored with a project, not personal memory. They apply when the Agent opens and reads that project's rules and do not automatically extend to other projects.

explanation.title: Conversation history
explanation.text: Belongs to a particular conversation. The system may provide it when that conversation resumes; retention depends on the session mechanism.

explanation.title: Project rules
explanation.text: Live in project files or settings. The Agent must actually read them in the target project for them to enter the current context.

explanation.title: Cross-session memory
explanation.text: A product may save and retrieve selected information in later interactions; there is no universal guarantee about what is saved or recalled.

data.boundary: Closing a window does not mean every product deletes conversation history; a new conversation does not guarantee a preference was saved or retrieved. Check what the target conversation actually loaded.

lessonPractice.title: Project rules in repository A say “do not automatically edit shared components.” You start a new conversation in repository B. How can you confirm the rule will apply?

options.label: Check the rules or memory loaded in this conversation; if missing, configure it for B or state it here, then verify
options.feedback: Correct. A file in repository A does not automatically apply in B; inspect what the new conversation actually received and add the requirement if needed.

options.label: Assume repository A's project rules also apply to B because it is the same AI product
options.feedback: Project rules are generally loaded with their project; using the same product does not mean repository A's file is automatically read in another repository.

options.label: Assume the Agent remembers the rule because it handled a similar task before
options.feedback: A similar past task does not prove the preference was saved or retrieved in this turn; inspect what the new conversation received.

data.agentPrompt: This new conversation must also follow “do not automatically edit shared components.” First tell me which project rules or memories you actually loaded for this turn. If the requirement is missing, add it to this project's rules or the current request before changing code.
